newsitem.title: HONG KONG: TABLE TENNIS-DENG CAPTURES FIRST WORLD CUP TITLE.
newsitem.headline: TABLE TENNIS-DENG CAPTURES FIRST WORLD CUP TITLE.

text.p: Olympic champion Deng Yaping won the first women's table tennis World Cup singles title on Monday with a straight-games win over Chinese compatriot Yang Ying.

Deng, gold medallist in both singles and doubles at the Atlanta Olympics, defeated 19-year-old world number six Yang 21-18 21-18 21-17 in an entertaining match which was largely a stroll for the top-ranked Deng.

She was overwhelming favourite to win the US$22,000 first prize, the richest on the women's circuit, after Taiwan's Chen Jing and China's Qiao Hong, the Olympic silver and bronze medallists, turned down invitations to compete.
Deng said after her win she would cut back her international playing commitments and give preference to her university studies.
She said the time was ripe for China's new generation, led by Yang and third-place finisher Wang Chen, to challenge for the major titles.
"I am very happy that the young ones are coming up now. In the future China will be relying on them," Deng said.
She said she would concentrate on her business management studies at Qinghua University in Beijing but would definitely defend her world title in Manchester next year.
"I am going to study a lot more but I will be taking part in the world championships," she said. "But I have not decided about the Asian Games (in 1998 in Bangkok). That is too far ahead."
In the semifinals Deng overpowered Sweden's Marie Svensson, the 1994 European champion, 21-13 21-14 21-11 while Yang defeated compatriot Wang Chen, the world number five, 21-18 21-15 21-5.
Wang took third place, taking advantage of lapses in Svensson's game to win the play-off 23-21 21-15.
